line-chart-standard-example: A standard example of the line chart. The static dataset has a fixed size (400 x 400). The active/focused line is pulled in front of other non-active lines. (synthetic z-index for SVG elements).
line-chart-flat-datasets: A standard example of the line chart but with fully flat datasets, try to navigate with arrows keyboard navigation.
stacked-line-chart-description: Stacked line chart. Each series value is calculated based on the previous series in the series array.
svg-chart-resize: SVG charts always require width and height values. In order to track parent size you can use ParentSize helper. Try to resize the following chart (drag any corner of the chart block).
resize-logic-note: Note: Resize logic comes from react-resize package and not from this chart package.
chart-layout-fixed-size: The following chart layout (chart and legend blocks) has a fixed size of 400x400. Chart size is calculated (Chart = ParentSize - LegendSize).
unaligned-data-series: With unaligned by (x and y axes) data series
tooltip-existing-points: It's a possible situation when some series has fewer points than others on the chart. In this case, we just show only existing points in the tooltip.
line-charts-short-datasets-issue: Currently, line charts and axis components may not handle short datasets properly. This is something that we want to improve in the future.
interpolation-unaligned-datasets: In case some datasets are unaligned, the stacked value will take the closest points of previous data series, interpolate values and apply a synthetically calculated value as a basis for the current series point.
interpolation-formula: X = D (interpolation between S and E) + X (value)
